topic: Texas transplant reality check across San Antonio, Austin, DFW
hook: I moved 14 miles closer and lost 20 minutes.

scores.worst_problem: The first loop, "The cheaper address costs more," just re-states the slide it sits on rather than pointing forward at the tax-rate reveal, so the strongest slide ends without pull.
scores.fix: Rewrite loop 1 to point at the next idea instead of summarising this one — something like "Miles aren't the worst number" — and drop "Save this for later" so the closing question is the only ask.

deck.topic: Texas transplant reality check across San Antonio, Austin, DFW
deck.hook: I moved 14 miles closer and lost 20 minutes.

points.title: The 14 Mile Trap
body: I cut 14 miles off my Austin drive and it cost me 20 minutes each way.
The new route crossed a highway that stacks up at 7:40 and never recovers.
In Texas you commute the chokepoints, not the mileage.

points.title: Rate, Not Price
body: No state income tax gets all the attention. The property tax rate is the part that actually moves.
Two nearly identical houses, opposite sides of one line, and the annual bills are thousands apart.
People shop list price and never pull the rate.

points.title: Districts Lie, Boundaries Don't
body: Especially around DFW. One district name covers campuses that look nothing alike.
And boundaries get redrawn when a few hundred new roofs go up.
Buy the attendance zone. Not the logo on the water tower.

points.title: Two Weeks Run The Year
body: Fifty weeks here are genuinely great. Two of them decide how you feel about the house.
One stretch of triple digits and one freeze week where pipes and power get tested.
Ask about shade orientation, attic work, and how the place handled the last freeze.

points.title: The 90 Minute Circle
body: Every transplant says they will drive anywhere. By month three, weekends live inside 90 minutes.
San Antonio buys you Hill Country and a shot at the coast. Austin buys you rivers and lakes close in. DFW weekends run toward water east and quiet south.
Pick the city whose 90 minute circle you actually want.

linkedinCaption:
Four years of relocation clients and the same five surprises keep coming up. None of them show up in a listing.

Mileage does not predict commute time in Texas. Chokepoints do. I cut 14 miles off an Austin drive and added 20 minutes each way.

No state income tax gets the headlines. The property tax rate is what actually changes the math, and two nearly identical houses on opposite sides of one line can be thousands apart annually.

District names mean less than attendance zones, especially in DFW. Boundaries move when the roofs go up.

Fifty weeks here are great. The heat stretch and the freeze week decide how you feel about the house.

What do you wish buyers understood about your market before they toured anything?
